schema.description:
Structured fields pulled from the raw intake document (Component 1: Intelligent
Document Intake). Diagnosis/procedure codes must be taken verbatim, never inferred.

patient_id.description: Patient identifier as it appears in the document
patient_id.title: Patient Id

date_of_birth.description: Patient date of birth, as written in the document
date_of_birth.title: Date Of Birth

diagnosis_codes.description: ICD-10 codes exactly as they appear, never inferred
diagnosis_codes.title: Diagnosis Codes

procedure_codes.description: CPT/HCPCS codes exactly as they appear in the request
procedure_codes.title: Procedure Codes

clinical_notes.description: Verbatim relevant clinical narrative preserved from the document
clinical_notes.title: Clinical Notes

urgency.description: routine / urgent / stat, inferred from clinical context
urgency.title: Urgency

confidence_score.description: Extraction confidence (document/OCR clarity), as a number from 0.0 to 1.0
confidence_score.title: Confidence Score

extraction_notes.description: Anything ambiguous or low-confidence about this extraction
extraction_notes.title: Extraction Notes

schema.title: ExtractedRequest

messages.content:
You are the document-intake extraction agent in a prior-authorization pipeline for a regional health plan. You will be given the raw text of a prior authorization request (from a fax, PDF, portal submission, or provider upload).

Extract the structured fields exactly as specified. Rules:
- Diagnosis codes (ICD-10) and procedure codes (CPT/HCPCS) must be taken VERBATIM from the text. Never infer or guess a code that is not explicitly written down. If none are present, return an empty list for that field.
- Preserve the clinically relevant narrative verbatim in clinical_notes (you may trim obvious boilerplate/header noise, but do not paraphrase clinical content).
- urgency must reflect what the document actually says or clearly implies (e.g. "STAT", "urgent", explicit time pressure) — default to "routine" if nothing indicates otherwise.
- confidence_score reflects how clearly and unambiguously the document text supports this extraction (document/OCR clarity), NOT your opinion of the clinical case. Use lower scores if text is garbled, fields are ambiguous, or required fields are simply absent.
- Use extraction_notes to flag anything ambiguous, contradictory, or low-confidence.

Raw intake document text:

*** PDF UPLOAD — PRIOR AUTHORIZATION REQUEST ***
Submitted via Provider Portal (PDF attachment, text extracted)

Patient ID: MEM-65590212
Patient Name: T. Boateng (synthetic demo patient)
Date of Birth: 01/30/1990

Requesting Provider: Dr. Elena Petrov, MD — Riverside Orthopedic Associates
Ordering NPI: 1620394857

Diagnosis Code(s): S83.241A (Medial meniscus tear, current injury), M25.561 (Pain in right knee)
Procedure Code(s) Requested: 29881 (Knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy)

Urgency: Routine

Clinical Notes:
32-year-old with right knee pain and intermittent mechanical locking for the past 8 weeks
following a twisting injury while playing recreational soccer. MRI right knee (reviewed
6/2/2026) showed a medial meniscus tear consistent with symptoms. Patient completed a 5-week
course of physical therapy and NSAIDs with only partial improvement; mechanical locking
persists and is now affecting activities of daily living. Physical exam notes joint line
tenderness and positive McMurray test. No prior knee surgery. No absolute contraindications to
surgery documented.

Note: exact date physical therapy was completed is not specified in this submission (referenced
generally as "5-week course" without start/end dates).
